validated_results.title: Serum levels of selenium and smoking habits at age 50 influence long term prostate cancer risk; a 34 year ULSAM follow-up.
validated_results.reason: Prospective population-based cohort measuring serum selenium at age 50 with registry-confirmed incident prostate cancer over 34 years, providing a quantitative selenium-related hazard ratio.

extraction.comparison_type: Smokers with serum selenium in the two lower tertiles (≤80 μg/L) versus smokers in the high selenium tertile
extraction.population: Population-based Swedish male cohort investigated at age 50

sample_size.excerpt: ULSAM, a population based Swedish male cohort (n = 2322) investigated at age 50 for s-Se and s-Se influencing factors: serum cholesterol, erythrocyte sedimentation rate and smoking habits.

cases.excerpt: In a 34-year-follow-up, national registries identified 208 PrCa cases further confirmed in medical records.

effect_size.excerpt: Smokers with s-Se in the two lower tertiles (≤80 μg/L) experienced a higher cumulative incidence of PrCa than smokers in the high selenium tertile (Hazard Ratio 2.39; 95% CI: 1.09-5.25). A high tertile selenium level in combination with non-wt rs125701 of the OGG1 gene in combination with smoking status or rs4880 related variation of MnSOD gene appeared to protect from PrCa.

confidence_interval.excerpt: Smokers with s-Se in the two lower tertiles (≤80 μg/L) experienced a higher cumulative incidence of PrCa than smokers in the high selenium tertile (Hazard Ratio 2.39; 95% CI: 1.09-5.25).

validated_results.title: Vitamin E and the risk of prostate cancer: the Selenium and Vitamin E Cancer Prevention Trial (SELECT).
validated_results.reason: Randomized placebo-controlled trial of selenium supplementation with prostate cancer incidence as the primary outcome.

extraction.comparison_type: Oral selenium 200 μg/d from L-selenomethionine versus placebo
extraction.location: 427 study sites in the United States, Canada, and Puerto Rico
extraction.population: Relatively healthy men aged 50 years or older (black men) or 55 years or older with PSA ≤4.0 ng/mL

sample_size.excerpt: The primary analysis included 34,887 men who were randomly assigned to 1 of 4 treatment groups: 8752 to receive selenium; 8737, vitamin E; 8702, both agents, and 8696, placebo.

cases.excerpt: Compared with the placebo (referent group) in which 529 men developed prostate cancer, 620 men in the vitamin E group developed prostate cancer (hazard ratio [HR], 1.17; 99% CI, 1.004-1.36, P = .008); as did 575 in the selenium group (HR, 1.09; 99% CI, 0.93-1.27; P = .18), and 555 in the selenium plus vitamin E group (HR, 1.05; 99% CI, 0.89-1.22, P = .46).

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with the placebo (referent group) in which 529 men developed prostate cancer, 620 men in the vitamin E group developed prostate cancer (hazard ratio [HR], 1.17; 99% CI, 1.004-1.36, P = .008); as did 575 in the selenium group (HR, 1.09; 99% CI, 0.93-1.27; P = .18), and 555 in the selenium plus vitamin E group (HR, 1.05; 99% CI, 0.89-1.22, P = .46). Compared with placebo, the absolute increase in risk of prostate cancer per 1000 person-years was 1.6 for vitamin E, 0.8 for selenium, and 0.4 for the combination.
